newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close higher on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close higher on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed higher on Tuesday on bargain-hunting of selected medium- and big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 2.59 points, or 0.48 percent, to close at 545.11 points. Losers led gainers by 50 to 48, with 54 counters unchanged.
"Overall trading was moderate but market sentiment remains volatile. Today's rebound is only technical because prevailing price of some stocks were at bargain levels," one broker said.
But brokers said the cheap prices were unlikely to lead to a sustained rally as many foreign players have not regained confidence following a surge in political tensions in the summer.
Brokers said bargain hunting of blue-chips Gudang Garam and Sampoerna and positive news on selected secondliners had pushed the composite index up.
Property firm Bhuwanatala IP topped the active list with 10.5 million shares traded, rising 50 rupiah to 1,300 rupiah after it touched 1,350 rupiah in early trade.
Brokers ascribed the rise to market talk that the firm was likely to be awarded two property projects.
Oil and natural gas explorer firm Medco Energy rose 375 rupiah, or 15.96 percent, to 2,725 rupiah on a volume of 10.4 million shares.
Brokers said the sharp rise was due to news that the company had found additional oil sources in South Sumatra.
